newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Friday, with most rates remaining at high levels due to increased fund demand by financial institutions at the year-end, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 22.10 percent from 20.01 percent on Thursday.
Combined turnover fell to 7.96 million lots from 10.37 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Most financial institutions need more money for year-end settlement," said one trader. "This has prompted some to borrow on the repo market to trade on the (domestic) A share markets."
"Reduced trading volume indicated fund supply on the repo market was insufficient," said a second trader. Traders expect the repo rates to remain at high levels in the short term.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed, with four contracts up, four down and one flat. Traders said investor confidence was weak after months of falls.
The most active three-year bond that matures in September 1999 edged up to 101.67 yuan from 101.36 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market shrank to 1.02 million lots from 1.53 million.
"Volume continued to shrink today, partly because major institutions have become less and less interested in spot trading," said one trader.
Traders said the spot market was unlikely to recover in the short term due to poor market sentiment and a shortage of funds among financial institutions in the short term.
